infra-bot: [ALERT] elevated apiserver 5xx in us-west1 - spike started ~15:10 UTC; approx 95 5xx/min over 6m; affected components: apiserver-proxy, attach-controller :rotating_light:
maya: noticed high attach latencies from provisioner (us-west1-gpu pool). controller-manager threads stuck on attach RPCs, causing watch reconnections and leader election chatter.
jess: seeing etcd leader stepdown events correlated with high apiserver latency, leader transferred at 15:12 and again at 15:18.
maya: logs (provisioner):
```
W0316 15:11:58.332 attach.go:142] attach request timeout to attach-service (POST /attach) err: dial tcp: i/o timeout
E0316 15:12:02.551 provisioner.go:670] attach failed for pod redwood/gpu-train-abc: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = unexpected EOF
I0316 15:12:05.100 provisioner.go:682] requeue node gpu-node-pool-12 (backoff=8s)
```
bryce: any cloud-side notes?
anya: cloud support shows transient SNAT port exhaustion on the NAT gateway for that subnet from 15:08-15:16; they reported cleared at 15:17. We also had a sudden burst of new pods during a scheduled canary for gpu-training (HPA scaled from 5->50).
sam: controller-manager metric `workqueue_depth{controller="attach-controller"}` jumped 4->380 in ~4m. `apiserver_request_duration_seconds` p95 jumped to ~9.4s.
maya: consequence: apiserver proxy goroutines blocked waiting for attach responses causing request queuing; with apiserver p95 high, etcd sees increased request retries and leader churn.
jess: quick mitigations we can do now:
- pause HPA for the canary (scale to 2)
- cordon new nodes that are still provisioning to stop more attach attempts
- reduce controller-manager `--concurrent-syncs` for attach controller to reduce parallel attaches (tradeoff slower clearance vs fewer SNATs)
- enable apiserver `--max-requests-inflight` tuning to reserve threads for non-proxy traffic
maya: doing HPA pause now: `kubectl scale hpa gpu-training-canary -n redwood --replicas=2`
```
kubectl scale hpa/gpu-training-canary -n redwood --replicas=2
```
infra-bot: action logged: HPA scale request at 15:20 by maya.
anya: also recommend prewarming a small pool of ready nodes with attached GPUs (no CNIs causing SNAT) for rapid onboarding windows. Cost impact < $0.02/node/hr but prevents these storms.
bryce: network option: we can switch attach RPCs to use internal VPC paths (east-west LB) to bypass NAT entirely but requires firewall and LB rule change; estimated 1.5h change window.
sam: short-term plan: pause canary HPA, cordon nodes with attach failures, run a targeted requeue for stalled items with longer backoff, and watch `attach_controller_errors_total`. If we still see apiserver 5xx after backlog drains, escalate to cloud network.
jess: I kicked a job to drain workqueue items that have >3 failures and reset backoff: `./adminctl requeue --controller attach --reset-backoff --filter failures>3`
maya: executing cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-pool-12-abc -n kube-system`
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-pool-12-abc
```
infra-bot: cordon action recorded at 15:22 by maya.
anya: monitoring created: temporary alert `attach_controller_stuck` firing when workqueue_depth > 100 for 5m and attach_latency_p95 > 3s. paging threshold set.
bryce: follow-ups: 1) write runbook step to limit HPA spike during GPU-onboarding windows, 2) cost estimate for east-west LB, 3) consider opening /29->/27 for NAT expansion if LB not feasible.
sam: I'll stay on this and update in 20m. if leader churn continues, we'll need to coordinate etcd maintenance window (avoid heavy writes) and possibly bump etcd election timeout temporarily.
maya: noted. adding @jess to postmortem draft and runbook edits. thanks team. :thumbsup:
